To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

preoperative fasting is a simple, non-invasive intervention that improves renal function and survival after ischemia/reperfusion injury in mice of both sexes, of different genetic background, and of different age and body weight.

fasting before surgery improves kidney function and survival after renal ischemia-reperfusion in aged and overweight mice of both genders, which may indicate a potential benefit for older and overweight patients undergoing renal surgery.
Preoperative fasting in aged-overweight F1 mice protects against renal ischemia-reperfusion-injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether preoperative fasting protects from ischemia-reperfusion injuries in the kidney.
the effects of pre-operative fasting on renal ischemia-reperfusion-injury (IRI) in mice.
the development and application of a new method for the treatment of acute kidney failure, which is a major problem in the treatment of critically ill patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fasting is a promising intervention in the treatment of renal IRI.
fasting is beneficial for all patients, regardless of age, body weight and gender.
preoperative fasting protects renal tissue against IRI and therefore improves survival and kidney function in mice, regardless of age, weight, sex and genetic background.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
preoperative fasting protects the kidney from ischemia-reperfusion damage in mice.
fasting induces a metabolic switch from glucose to ketones and fatty acids.
fasting protects against IRI and is therefore beneficial in patients before surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preoperative fasting is a non-invasive and safe intervention that can be applied to protect patients against renal ischemia reperfusion injury (I/R).
preoperative fasting protects the kidney against ischemia-reperfusion in older and overweight mice of both sexes.
fasting is an easy, inexpensive and non-invasive intervention to protect against ischemia-reperfusion induced injury.
